channel.title: Skyline Vanguard — The Commute Briefing
channel.description: A daily ~20-minute editorial briefing for real-estate and insurance professionals, hosted by Tawny & Paul — mortgage rates, insurance regulation, real-estate transactions, construction, and business opportunity, pulled from Skyline Roofing's Vanguard newspaper.

item.title: Vanguard Commute Briefing — Oct 8, 2026
item.description:
Welcome to the Skyline Vanguard Daily Briefing — the twenty-minute commute podcast for real estate and insurance professionals. I'm Tawny. And I'm Paul. Good morning. Here's what matters today. Property tax delinquency just hit its highest rate since twenty seventeen. A catastrophe modeler is updating its storm model with new roof-age data that changes how carriers will underwrite. Hive MLS is adding a buyer listing service that lets agents see demand before a property ever hits the market.

item.title: Vanguard Commute Briefing — Oct 4, 2026
item.description:
So the FHFA is planning to direct Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to shift from tri-merge credit reports to bi-merge. What does that actually mean? Right, so instead of lenders pulling credit reports from all three bureaus — Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion — they'd select two of the three. According to HousingWire reporting October first, this is expected to be formally announced as soon as October twelfth, possibly at the Mortgage Bankers Association conference in Chicago.
Full edition: https://flipbooks.skylineroofllc.com/social-test/vanguard-video-2026-10-04/

item.title: Vanguard Commute Briefing — Sep 28, 2026
item.description:
The thirty-year fixed mortgage rate just crossed seven point one two percent in the week ended September eighteenth. That's the highest level since May twenty twenty-four, and it's the first real jolt in rates we've seen in months. According to the Mortgage Bankers Association's Weekly Applications Survey, the seasonally adjusted Purchase Index fell one percent week-over-week. But the year-over-year numbers are worse — the unadjusted Purchase Index is eleven percent lower than a year ago.
